meaning: Coverage records locate knowledge to study. They do not assert that the student has studied, practised or mastered it. Question-level scores are separate.

clauses.summary: Rational, negative and integer index laws; common-base equations.
Surd simplification and rationalising with conjugates.
Quadratic solution methods, square completion, discriminant and graph-root interpretation.

Analytic substitution and elimination are taught explicitly in the additional simultaneous-equations concept, with a line–quadratic worked example retaining and checking both coordinate pairs; the graphical concept interprets the intersections.
Linear/quadratic inequalities, signs and interval boundaries.
Expansion, factorisation, rational manipulation, linear/quadratic polynomial division, Factor and Remainder Theorems. Repeated linear factors record root multiplicities and their sign parity.
One-output function definition, one-to-one/many-to-one, principal square roots and modulus; mapping definition already appears in P2 B1 p2 starter, now catalogued.
Position rules, recurrences, periodicity and explicit linear/quadratic nth terms.
P1 Booklet 1 Lesson 8, p11, teaches arithmetic sums and explicitly gives 1+2+...+n=n(n+1)/2, with inclusive term counts and differences of partial sums.
Finite geometric sums and convergent infinite sums with absolute ratio below one.

Positive-integer binomial expansion, coefficient selection, factorial and combination notation. The additional factorial concept teaches the product meaning, nonnegative-integer input domain, zero boundary value and recurrence required by the stated factorial notation; no binomial-selection operation is inferred merely from a factorial expression.
Line equations, parallel/perpendicular gradients and geometric special cases.
Both circle equation forms, centres, radii, diameter endpoints.
All seven listed chord/tangent/circle-angle properties.

Sine/cosine rules, included-angle area, SSA ambiguity and 3D reduction. The sine rule supports the separately taught angle/side-order theorem; the result is derived rather than quoted as a named clause.
Radian arc length, sector and segment area.
Exact standard-angle trigonometric values; tangent at 90° is undefined.
Sine/cosine/tangent graphs, ranges, symmetries and periods. First-quarter sine monotonicity and sine symmetry justify angle/side ordering even when the larger angle is obtuse.
tan=sin/cos where defined, and sin²+cos²=1.
All branches in a stated interval, identity reductions and endpoint checks.
Positive-base exponential graphs, growth/decay and constant-base-one case.
Log definition, product/quotient/power laws, reciprocal/own-base cases and domains; no change-of-base requirement.
Exponential equations, common bases and hidden quadratic substitution.
Derivative/tangent interpretation, rates and units, first/second-derivative notation; no first-principles requirement.
Differentiate rational powers and sums after simplification.

Tangents, normals, maxima/minima and strict derivative-sign monotonicity; zero derivative need not be an extremum. Factor-sign reasoning classifies local maxima/minima; the published exclusion of inflexion questions remains unchanged.
Signed definite integrals distinguished from geometric area.
Power antiderivatives for rational exponents other than −1, simplification and bounds.
Fundamental theorem in antiderivative evaluation and accumulated-integral differentiation forms.
Combine/split equal or contiguous intervals and reverse limits.
Trapezium-rule calculation and chord-position over/underestimate assessment.
Solve dy/dx=f(x) by integration and determine the constant from given information.
Recognise required line, quadratic, cubic, trig, log, exponential, square-root and modulus shapes.
Input/output translations, stretches, reflections, composed transformations and f(g(x)).
Explicit effects of gradient m and intercept c on y=mx+c.

P1 Booklet 1 Lessons 3 and 12, pp5 and 15, combine completed-square vertices with translations, vertical scaling and reflection. Applied to y=a(x+b)^2+c for nonzero a, these locate the vertex (-b,c), set the opening by the sign of a and scale vertical displacement by |a|.
Derivative signs and stationary heights determine graph shape and crossings.
Axis intersections, polynomial real-root counts and repeated-root boundaries. Distinct root locations and repeated-factor multiplicities are distinguished when counting degree.
Equations correspond to graph intersections, including approximate numerical read-offs.
Standard measures and compound speed, pay/unit pricing, density and pressure; graph rates/totals supply contextual units.
Convert related simple and compound units; square/cube length conversion factors where needed.
Ordering signed integers, decimals and fractions; comparison symbols and equality boundaries.
Place value and the four operations with signed decimals, fractions and mixed numbers.
Prime factors, product powers, uniqueness, HCF and LCM; existing integer-proof and HCF-invariance coverage retained.
Inverse operations, cancellation, brackets, operation priority, powers, roots and reciprocals.
Systematic choices and multiplication principle, including prescribed positions and ordered outcomes.
Squares/cubes and roots, including the distinction between principal square-root notation and two equation roots.
Numerical integer, negative and fractional index laws.
Standard form is already defined and worked in P1 B4 p21; expand the existing summary rather than duplicate the card.
Terminating decimal/fraction/percentage conversion plus new recurring-decimal conversion.
Equivalent fractions and interchangeable fraction/decimal/percentage calculations.
Exact fraction/surd/pi calculations and rationalising denominators.
Upper/lower bounds in contextual products, differences and quotients.
Decimal-place/significant-figure rounding, truncation and correct error-interval endpoints already taught; expand summary.

P1 Booklet 4 Lesson 7, p21, teaches estimation with rounded decimals; additional learning explicitly extends this to approximate calculations containing pi and square roots, distinguishing rough estimates from exact values and proved bounds.
Scale factors, maps and scale drawings.
Quantity as a fraction of another, including ratios greater than one.
Ratio notation and its translation into equations.
Divide a whole using the sum of ratio parts and recover ratios from parts.
Ratio in mixtures, concentrations, conversions and comparisons.
Proportion, ratio-as-fraction and direct-proportion line through origin.
Work with fractions of totals in ratio and mixture problems.
Percent as parts per hundred, comparisons, >100%, changes, original values and simple interest.
Direct/inverse power proportion equations and their graph interpretation.
Length/area/volume scale factors and similarity links.
Growth/decay, compound interest and iterative processes.
Read multiplication, powers and fraction notation explicitly.
Algebraic integer, fractional and negative index laws.
Substitute values into expressions/formulae and use the required algebra vocabulary.
Collect terms, expand brackets/products and take common factors.
Factor monic and nonmonic quadratics, including differences of squares.

P1 Booklet 1 Lessons 1 and 5 teach factorisation/cancellation, a rational-expression subtraction exercise and index simplification. Additional learning explicitly covers all four rational-expression operations, common denominators, reciprocal division and original domain exclusions.
Rearrange formulae to isolate a requested subject with exclusions retained.
Equation versus identity and equivalence by valid algebra.
Coordinates in all four quadrants and coordinate transformations.
Gradients/intercepts, line equations, parallel and perpendicular conditions.
Quadratic roots, axis intercepts and completed-square turning points.
Required line/quadratic/cubic/reciprocal/exponential/trigonometric graph families.
Nonstandard/contextual graphs, motion and approximate solutions.
Estimate/interpret gradients and areas, including nonlinear curves, motion and financial units.

Analytic substitution and elimination are taught explicitly in the additional simultaneous-equations concept, with a line–quadratic worked example retaining and checking both coordinate pairs; the graphical concept interprets the intersections.
Quadratic factorisation, square completion, formula and approximate graph roots.
One-variable intervals and newly explicit two-variable linear regions.
Generate terms from term-to-term, recurrence and nth-term rules.
Linear nth terms retained and second-difference quadratic derivation added.
Points, lines and segments; vertices, edges and planes; parallel/perpendicular lines and right angles; named and subtended angles; polygons, regularity, reflection symmetry and rotational symmetry.

Angles at a point and on a straight line; perpendicular and vertically opposite angles; corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles for parallel lines; triangle and quadrilateral sums; polygon interior sums and exterior turning sums. The additional angle/side-order concept uses the triangle angle sum in its elementary proof; it does not replace the broader angle-properties coverage.

Definitions and derived side, angle and diagonal properties of squares, rectangles, parallelograms, trapezia, kites and rhombi; equilateral, isosceles, scalene, acute, right and obtuse triangles; regular plane polygons.
All four basic triangle congruence criteria: SSS, SAS with the included angle, ASA with corresponding angles and side, and RHS for right triangles.

Combine justified angle facts, congruence, similarity ratios and quadrilateral properties to prove conclusions about sides and angles. The additional angle/side-order concept derives and applies the within-triangle equivalence between a larger angle and a longer opposite side.

Identify, construct and describe congruent/similar coordinate shapes under rotation, reflection, translation and enlargement, including negative/fractional factors; compositions and invariant lengths/angles; translation by two-dimensional vectors.

Pythagoras with the hypotenuse correctly identified; two-dimensional right triangles, face diagonals and successive right triangles for three-dimensional distances. The surface-route application unfolds flat adjacent faces before applying Pythagoras, as in official 2016 Paper 1 Question 20.
Circle centre, radius, diameter, chord, circumference, tangent and arc; sectors versus segments; minor and major arcs, sectors and segments.

All named circle results: centre angle twice circumference angle; semicircle right angle; same-segment angles; tangent/chord alternate-segment theorem; radius perpendicular to tangent; cyclic-quadrilateral angles, with applications and justifications.
Coordinate geometry problems using distances, midpoints, gradients, perpendicular/parallel lines, circle equations and coordinate transformations.
Faces, curved surfaces, edges and vertices applied to cubes/cuboids, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, spheres and hemispheres; distinguish a flat face, curved surface and apex.
Plans and elevations of three-dimensional shapes, including footprints and overlapping stacks viewed from a stated direction.
Map and scale-drawing lengths, real distances and scale factors; bearings measured clockwise from north and written with three figures.
Recall and apply area formulae for triangles, parallelograms and trapezia, and volumes of cuboids and other right prisms using perpendicular height/length.

Circle circumference and area, right-cylinder volume; full perimeters and composite plane areas; exposed surface areas and volumes of composite solids; apply supplied sphere, pyramid and cone formulae.
Arc length, sector angle and sector area, including conversion between degree and radian measures and selection of the intended minor/major region.
Congruent and similar figures; corresponding length ratios, squared area ratios and cubed volume ratios, including the distinction between signed enlargement factor and positive length scale.

Explicit sine/cosine/tangent right-triangle ratios; angles and lengths in right and general triangles and in suitable planes within 3D figures; exact sine/cosine values for 0, 30, 45, 60, 90 degrees and tangent values for 0, 30, 45, 60 degrees.
Vector addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication in diagrams and column notation; displacement, collinearity and parallelism arguments and geometric proofs.

Read, construct and select categorical two-way/frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts and pictograms; vertical line charts for ungrouped discrete numerical data; tables and chronological line graphs for time series.
Read and construct grouped-data histograms with equal/unequal intervals and cumulative-frequency graphs; choose a suitable representation and use frequency density with area equal to frequency.

Exact ungrouped mean, mode, median and range; modal class and grouped estimates of mean, mode, median, range, quartiles and IQR from tables/graphs; why grouping loses exact values; population descriptions and like-for-like comparisons, including advantages/limitations of mean, median, range and IQR.

Scatter graphs for paired data; positive/negative/no linear correlation and the distinction from causation; draw an estimated best-fit line; interpolate and extrapolate while recognising uncertainty and the greater risk outside observed values.
Analyse experimental outcome frequencies in a table or frequency tree, preserve the correct trial total and verify branch counts sum to their parent.
Randomness, fair models and equally likely elementary outcomes; expected count Np across future experiments; actual repeated-batch outcomes may differ from each other and from their expectation.
Relate relative expected frequency p and observed relative frequency to theoretical probability; use estimate/expected/certain/impossible appropriately on the 0-to-1 scale.

Exhaustive elementary outcomes have total probability one; mutually exclusive exhaustive event groups also sum to one; find missing probabilities and complements while avoiding overlap double counting.
Systematic enumeration with lists/tables, sample-space grids, tree diagrams and disjoint Venn regions; combined sets/outcomes without assuming formal set-theory notation.

Construct equally likely theoretical possibility spaces for a single selection and combined experiments, then divide favourable counts by total counts while distinguishing elementary outcomes from unequal-probability totals.

Add mutually exclusive routes and multiply conditional branch probabilities; interpret conditional denominators via two-way tables, Venn regions and expected-frequency trees; distinguish independent branches from dependent draws with updated counts.
Truth, inclusive or, and, not; implication, if/only if/iff, converse and contrapositive.
Necessary and sufficient conditions with independent direction checks.
Universal and existential quantifiers, including order and domain.
Negate compound statements, implications and quantifiers.
Counterexample, direct deduction, exhaustive cases and contradiction.
Deduce valid implications and combine constraints.
Use small cases to formulate a conjecture, then justify it generally.
Reorder proof steps by their logical dependencies.
Connect several justified reasoning steps across a problem.
Identify the first unjustified step and explain why it fails.
Invalid cancellation, non-reversible operations, lost cases and false injectivity.
